description: Drive a WLED LED strip from video content playing in Jellyfin
name: WLED TV
overview: Server-side edge lighting for WLED. Jellyfin decodes the playing video with its bundled ffmpeg (hardware-accelerated, HDR tone-mapped), samples the edges of each frame, and streams the colours to a WLED strip in real time. No browser involvement, so it works on any client, including smart-TV apps.

versions.changelog:
## v2.1.0 — Jellyfin 12 support

Jellyfin 12 moved the server to **.NET 10**, which stops plugins built for Jellyfin 10.x from loading. This release ships builds for **both** generations.

### Added
- **Jellyfin 12 support.** One release, two builds — the catalogue offers the right one for your server automatically:

  | Your Jellyfin | Version you'll see | Build |
  |---|---|---|
  | 10.11.9+ | `2.1.0.10` | .NET 9 |
  | 12 | `2.1.0.12` | .NET 10 |

- The **4th version component is the Jellyfin major version** the build targets. This is deliberate: Jellyfin only offers an update when the catalogue version is *higher* than what's installed, so upgrading your server from 10.x to 12 now shows `2.1.0.12` as a normal plugin update and installs it automatically. Without it you'd silently keep the .NET 9 build and the plugin would fail to load.

No functional changes to edge lighting; this is a compatibility release.

## v2.0.2.0

### Sync delay is now bidirectional
- The **Sync delay** setting accepts **negative values** (−5000…5000 ms) and is now a **slider** with a live readout. Positive pushes the LEDs **later**; negative pulls them **earlier**.
- Under the hood the decoder no longer uses `-re` — it's paced by the read buffer instead, which primes quickly and keeps a bounded read-ahead. That removes the small residual output lag at delay 0 (so 0 is a true baseline) and gives the server already-decoded future frames to release early when you set a negative delay.
- **Tuning:** if the lighting runs *ahead* of the video, increase the slider; if it lags *behind*, drag it into the negative range.

### Fixed
- **LEDs sometimes stayed lit after returning to the menu** — the "off" message could race the last colour frame on the single-send WebSocket. Stopping now waits for the sender to fully stop before sending off (reconnecting first if needed), so the strip reliably goes dark.

## v2.0.1.0 — Proper A/V sync

Fixes the ambilight drifting out of sync with the picture (usually running early), which previously needed a manual pause/seek to reset.

### What changed
- **LED timing is now slaved to the TV's playback clock** instead of free-running on the decoder. Each frame carries its own timestamp; a clock model re-anchored on every playback-progress event tracks the reported position and **cannot drift**. Large jumps are treated as seeks and re-decoded; small corrections are eased in so nothing jumps.
- **New "Sync delay (ms)" setting** compensates for your TV's fixed display lag (buffering + processing). If the lighting runs **ahead** of the video, increase it; if it lags **behind**, decrease it. This is now the only sync knob, and it stays put because the drift is gone.

### Tuning
Start around a few hundred ms and adjust to taste — for the setup that reported ~1 s early, try **~900 ms**. The right value depends on the TV's picture mode (game/low-latency modes need less).

## v2.0.0.0 — Server-side edge lighting

A ground-up rewrite. Sampling now happens **on the Jellyfin server** instead of in the browser, so it works on **any client** — including smart-TV apps (LG WebOS 26, etc.) where the browser can no longer read the video surface.

### How it works now
- When the selected device plays a video, the server decodes it with its **bundled ffmpeg** (`-hwaccel auto`, paced to real time), samples the edges of each frame, and streams the colours to WLED over a WebSocket.
- **Only the selected device is sampled** — no extra decode is incurred for anyone else on the server.
- **HDR** (HDR10 / HLG) content is **tone-mapped to SDR** so the LED colours match the screen.
- Playback **position, pause and seek** are followed via Jellyfin's session events so the lighting stays matched to the picture; the strip turns off when playback stops.
- The letterbox/pillarbox and panel-aspect handling from before is preserved.

### Removed / changed settings
- **Removed:** *Sample depth* (now a fixed 1.5% inset), *Update interval* (one update per decoded frame, flow-controlled), *Video capture method* (no client capture anymore), and *Debug mode*.
- **Kept:** device, WLED URL, LED counts, start position, direction, brightness, batch updates, and the two letterbox/pillarbox toggles.
- The **Test** button now checks reachability from the **server** to WLED (the real runtime path).
- The **JavaScript Injector** plugin is **no longer required**.

### Requirements
- WLED must be reachable from the **Jellyfin server** (not just the browser).
- Hardware decoding enabled in Jellyfin is recommended, especially for 4K.

## v1.4.1.0

Reworks how letterbox/pillarbox handling maps the LEDs so they follow the picture as it actually appears on the panel.

### Fixed
- **LEDs now follow the on-screen picture, not the raw video frame.** The capture is the raw decoded video, so the black bars a 4:3 video shows on a 16:9 panel are never in the captured pixels — the compositor adds them on screen. The video's on-screen rectangle is now derived from the video-vs-panel aspect ratio, and LEDs over a bar stay dark instead of the picture being stretched across the whole strip.

### Toggle behaviour
- The LEDs over the black bars are **always** dark, regardless of the toggles.
- **Detect pillarboxing** controls the left/right strips: **on** maps them to the video's side edges (lit); **off** leaves them dark.
- **Detect letterboxing** controls the top/bottom strips: **on** maps them to the video's top/bottom (lit); **off** leaves them dark.
- Example — a 4:3 video on a 16:9 TV with pillarbox **off**: the sides stay dark and only the middle of the top/bottom strips light up; with pillarbox **on** the full sides light up too, mapped to the edges of the video.

Bars baked into the video file are handled the same way. The WebGL sampler (capture path) is unchanged.

## v1.4.0.0

Reworks letterbox/pillarbox detection to be more accurate and fully optional.

### Changed
- **Symmetric detection** — a bar is only detected when it appears on *both* opposing sides (using the smaller of the two). This fixes the case where one merely-dark side of the picture was wrongly detected as a boundary.
- **Aspect-ratio clamp** — letterboxing is capped at **21:9** and pillarboxing at **4:3**. Darker regions beyond that are treated as genuine content, not bars.
- **Content-aligned LEDs** — LEDs now map to where the picture actually is instead of stretching it across the whole strip. With pillarboxing the top/bottom LEDs light up only above/below the centred content; with letterboxing the side LEDs light up only alongside the content. The bar regions stay dark.

### Added
- **Detect letterboxing** and **Detect pillarboxing** settings — each toggles its dimension independently (both on by default).
